name: Unconstrained Delegation Abuse (Printer Bug + Rubeus)
description: Abuse unconstrained Kerberos delegation — when a DC connects to the compromised host, its TGT is cached and can be extracted to DCSync or impersonate the DC.

steps.label: On unconstrained host: start TGT monitor

recommended.note: DCSync once we have the DC TGT
Create golden ticket after krbtgt dump
Coerce the DC to authenticate (printerbug/DFSCoerce) to capture its TGT

notes: Requires SYSTEM on unconstrained host. SpoolService (printer bug) forces DC to authenticate back. Use Petitpotam as alternative trigger.

defense.why_it_works: When a computer account has unconstrained delegation enabled (TrustedForDelegation=True), any user authenticating to a service on that host has their full TGT forwarded to the service. If an attacker controls that host, they can extract those TGTs from LSASS and impersonate any user who connected — including Domain Admins. The Printer Bug (SpoolSample) forces a DC to authenticate to the attacker's host, delivering a DA-equivalent TGT.
defense.prerequisites: Control of a host with unconstrained delegation. Rubeus or Mimikatz to monitor and extract TGTs. SpoolSample or PetitPotam to coerce DC authentication. Local admin on the delegation host.
defense.impact: T1558 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets + T1187 Forced Authentication. Captures TGTs of any user authenticating to the host, including DCs. DA TGT → full domain compromise. Can also be used for Pass-the-Ticket after capture.
defense.detection:
Rubeus monitor output reveals incoming TGTs — not directly detectable. Event 4769 (TGS request) from DC to printer/spooler service on the delegation host (Printer Bug coercion). MDI: 'Suspected unconstrained delegation abuse'. Event 4624 type 3 on the delegation host from unexpected principals (DCs). Sysmon Event 3: outbound SMB from DC to a non-DC workstation (unusual).
Anomalous Kerberos activity: forged or stolen tickets by correlating malformed fields in logon events, RC4-encrypted TGTs, or TGS requests without corresponding TGT requests; suspicious processes accessing LSASS memory for ticket extraction (DET0522/AN1443).
Suspicious access to SSSD secrets database and Kerberos key material indicating ticket theft or replay; correlate anomalous file access with unusual Kerberos service ticket requests (AN1444).
Forging or replaying Kerberos tickets: monitor Unified Logs for anomalous kinit/klist activity and unusual authentication sequences (AN1445).
defense.artifacts: Event 4769 on DC: TGS for CIFS/host to delegation host | Sysmon Event 3: DC → delegation host TCP 445 (Printer Bug) | MDI: unconstrained delegation abuse alert | Event 4624 type 3 on delegation host from DC machine account | TGTs in LSASS on delegation host
defense.prevention:
Audit and remove unnecessary unconstrained delegation: Get-ADComputer -Filter {TrustedForDelegation -eq $true}. Replace with constrained delegation or resource-based constrained delegation (RBCD). Disable the Print Spooler service on DCs (blocks Printer Bug coercion). Add DCs and privileged accounts to Protected Users (tickets not forwardable). MDI deployment.
Active Directory Configuration: Reset KRBTGT account password twice (invalidates all golden tickets); rotate every 180 days.
Audit: Scan for insecure Kerberos configurations.
Credential Access Protection: On Linux, use SELinux to protect Kerberos key material.
Encrypt Sensitive Information: Enable AES Kerberos encryption instead of RC4.
Password Policies: Service accounts should have 25+ character passwords; use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA).
Privileged Account Management: Limit domain admin to DCs only; restrict service account privileges.
defense.evasion: Use PetitPotam or DFSCoerce as alternative coercion methods if Print Spooler is disabled. Extract tickets during a maintenance window when high auth activity reduces anomaly signal. Use the extracted TGT from memory (no disk artifact).
defense.misconfiguration: Computer accounts granted TrustedForDelegation=True unnecessarily (often old Exchange/SharePoint setups). Print Spooler enabled on DCs. DCs not in Protected Users (tickets forwardable).
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Find unconstrained delegation hosts:
Get-ADComputer -Filter {TrustedForDelegation -eq $true} -Properties TrustedForDelegation | Select-Object Name,TrustedForDelegation
# Output includes non-DC servers → VULNERABLE

# Print Spooler running on DC (enables Printer Bug coercion):
Get-Service -ComputerName DC01 -Name Spooler | Select-Object Status
# Running → VULNERABLE to forced auth via MS-RPRN
